This small plot of beans is close to my compound, so I will spread some of the manure from my animals on it before planting — that is what we always do for the legumes. I will not buy fertilizer for beans because beans do not need it the way millet or sorghum do, and money is tight. But the insects on the pods are bad every year, so I must spray pesticide, otherwise I will harvest nothing. I will use my own seed saved from last year, and my family will do most of the work, though I may pay a young man for two or three days to help with weeding since I am old now.
